That will create a race condition. RenderingServer should never be used as data storage for Scene-level objects because it runs async. Just cache the value in Viewport if you can reliably cache it.

This is because in the scaling mode of `CanvasItem`, the `Embed Window` needs to synchronize the scaling of the viewport texture size to avoid blurry rendering. However, according to the standard behavior of `CanvasItem` scaling, the size of the window itself should not change

Window size doesn't not change, but viewport size changes and is alwarys equal to the `ViewportTexture` size, no? I think `ViewportTexture.get_size` just needs to return `vp->size` like it was before #97745.

Edit: Actually `Window.size` changes when window resizing. In my opinion the relationship between them should be clarified before adding `texture_size` which complicates things.

> Edit: Actually `Window.size` changes when window resizing. In my opinion the relationship between them should be clarified before adding `texture_size` which complicates things.

In CanvasItem mode, when the main window is resized, the Window.size of the embedded window does not change. However, it needs to render a larger or smaller image based on the scaling of the main window. Therefore, the size of the viewport texture must change; otherwise, the embedded window's display will become blurry when the main window is enlarged.

The reason for directly using RS::get_singleton()->viewport_set_size instead of modifying Viewport.size is that I am unsure whether it corresponds to Window.size, and I am also uncertain whether Viewport.size should change. The implementation of embedded windows in version 4.x has introduced many issues...
